newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas called steady to up slightly.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas called steady to up slightly.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures were expected to open unchanged to up slightly Thursday following a relatively neutral AGA stock report last night and a mixed ACCESS session, industry sources said.
Early June over-the-counter trade ranged from $2.19 to $2.225 after settling Wednesday at $2.206 per million British thermal units.
On ACCESS, June drifted between $2.192 and $2.23 and last traded 0.9 cent higher at $2.215.
In the morning cash, Henry Hub was talked between $2.18 and $2.23, on either side of yesterday's range of $2.19-2.22.

The market had little reaction to last night's AGA data showing U.S. gas stocks rose last week by 62 bcf, in line with an earlier Reuter poll for a 55-65 bcf build. While overall stocks are still 219 bcf, or 27 percent, above year-ago, traders said they still lagged the historical average. Eastern storage, which gained 36 bcf last week, remained 119 bcf, or 34 percent, over 1996 levels.

Technical traders still pegged June support and resistance at $2.15 and $2.30, respectively. Major buying should emerge at the $2.05 double bottom, with good selling likely at the $2.43 contract high.

"There really isn't a lot of demand over the next five days, so I expect some pressure, but there's obvious support (in June) at $2.15-2.16 and we'll see if it has enough momentum to get through," a Midwest trader said.

In Wednesday's cash, Gulf Coast swing prices were steady to down slightly in the high-teens. Midcon pipes were little changed at about $2.00. New York city gate gas also held relatively steady in the mid-$2.40s.

Transco said maintenance on its Texas line was scheduled to be completed later today and the line should be fully restored by Friday. The line has a capacity of 600 mmcfd, of which about 400 mmcfd was still cut today.

Planned work on Mobil's Mary Ann gas processing plant in Coden, Ala., has cut the plant's total processing capacity of 380-390 mmcfd. About 120 mmcfd should be back by early next week, with the balance due back in three weeks.
Normal to slightly below-normal temperatures are expected for most of the nation into early next week. Western states were forecast to warm to above-normal during the period.
